questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Diminish
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Weaken**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"diminish"** means to make or become less; to reduce in size, importance, or intensity. (कम करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The medicine helped **diminish **the pain.
 
 
 
• **"Weaken" **refers to making something or someone less strong or powerful; to reduce in strength. (कमज़ोर करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The storm **weakened **before it reached the coast.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the synonym of **'diminish' **is **'weaken'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Demote **(पदावनत करना): To lower someone or something in rank or position.

 
 
• **Example:** He was **demoted **from manager to assistant.
 
 
 
• **Relegate **(निम्न श्रेणी में रखना): To assign to a lower position or less important role.
 
 
• **Example: **The team was **relegated **to the second division.
 
 
 
• **Prevent** (रोकना): To stop something from happening or someone from doing something.
 
 
• **Example:** The new law aims to **prevent **fraud.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) We are living / (B) here since / (C) the summer / (D) of last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'A'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the use of the verb "are living" is incorrect when used with the preposition "since".
 
• The present perfect continuous tense should be used with "since" to show an action that started in the past and is still continuing.
 
• The correct form should be "have been living" instead of "are living".
 
• The corrected sentence would be: *"We have been living here since the summer of last year."*

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct sentence: ***We have been living** here since the summer of last year.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Option 1 (A): *"We are living"* is grammatically correct but does not fit with the time duration indicated by "since".
 
• Option 2 (C): *"the summer"* is correct and does not contain any error.
 
• Option 4 (D): *"of last year"* is also correct and does not contain any error.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Suresh has been learning Tamil ________ two months.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'for'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **'for'** is used to indicate a period of time during which an action happens.
 
• In the given sentence, Suresh has been learning Tamil for a specific period, which is two months.
 
• Using **'for'** correctly indicates the duration of the activity.
 
• Other options do not correctly convey the duration of time in this context.

Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Suresh has been learning Tamil **for*__ *two months.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: 'from'** - This option is incorrect because 'from' is used to indicate the starting point of an action or event, not the duration.
 
• **Option 2: 'since'** - This option is incorrect because 'since' is used to indicate the starting point of an action that continues up to the present, not the duration.
 
• **Option 3: 'before'** - This option is incorrect because 'before' is used to indicate a point in time prior to another event, not the duration.

• The idiom **"fight fire with fire"** means to respond to an attack or a problem with similar tactics or methods. (आग का जवाब आग से देना)

 
 
• **Example: **When the competitor launched a negative ad campaign, the company decided to **fight fire with fire** and released their own series of aggressive ads.
 
 
 
• The idiom "fight fire with fire" fits in the context of the given sentence.
